subject: MSA acceptance wording for phased capacity & retrospective billing parity
messages:
From: Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@alturahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@alturahealth.com
Date: 2027-02-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: MSA language for phased capacity + retrospective billing parity

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Altura's engineering team wants to move forward with a phased capacity add (initial 20% uplift for Q2, scale to full commit in Q4). Our procurement group asked for two things before we route a change order for signature:

1) A clear acceptance/ops clause in the MSA that ties phased capacity releases to acceptance checkpoints (we propose acceptance window of 5 business days after provisioning).
2) A billing parity statement so that any retrospective reallocation of capacity (e.g., if we convert pilot nodes to committed nodes) is billed at the same agreed rate and not subject to a later pricing floor — procurement insists on this for audit.

Attached is a draft change order (Altura_Change_Order_v1.docx) that our PM circulated internally. Can your legal/procurement team propose exact redline language for the MSA so we can avoid back-and-forth? We want to get this signed by end of month.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Jenkins
Head of Infrastructure, Altura Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
To: Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@alturahealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: MSA language for phased capacity + retrospective billing parity

Michael — thanks for the clear ask and the draft. Looping in Jordan (commercial) and Laura (legal ops) to help tighten the MSA wording. Quick answers up front:

- We can add an acceptance schedule tied to each provisioning tranche. I want to propose an explicit 3-step acceptance flow: Provision -> Smoke tests by Altura (3 business days) -> Joint acceptance sign-off (2 business days). Total 5 business days as you suggested.
- For billing parity: Redwood's standard approach is to keep retrospective conversions at the committed rate provided there are no material usage pattern changes. We can commit to the parity language but need to pin the operational trigger and audit window (we usually allow a 30-day lookback for usage reconciliation).

Jordan — can you draft oriented commercial language for the Order Form and propose a short MSA clause that legal can review? Laura — see attached quick mark (redlines_20270216.pdf) with our initial suggestions.

I'll hold the change order routing until we have agreed language. If Altura wants, we can run a 30-min legal-commercial sync today.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>, Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@alturahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: MSA language for phased capacity + retrospective billing parity

Michael / Hannah — draft clause below that I think balances Altura's ask and Redwood's commercial guardrails. Happy to iterate.

--- Proposed MSA clause (commercial suggestion) ---
Phased Provisioning and Acceptance: For phased capacity adds, Redwood will provision the agreed tranche within the timeframes set forth in the applicable Order Form. Altura shall execute smoke tests within three (3) business days of provisioning and provide notice of acceptance or rejection. If Altura does not provide notice within three (3) business days, the tranche shall be deemed accepted. Following Altura's acceptance, both Parties will execute a joint acceptance confirmation within two (2) business days.

Billing Parity on Conversion: If Altura elects to convert provisioned capacity from a phased or pilot tranche to a committed tranche within ninety (90) days of provisioning, Redwood will apply the committed rate set forth in the Order Form retroactively to the date of provisioning, provided that (i) Altura's usage during the interim period does not exceed 125% of the forecasted usage for the tranche, and (ii) no material breach of the Agreement has occurred. Any usage beyond the 125% threshold will be billed at the standard overage rate in effect at the time of usage.

--- end clause ---

Laura — this drafts the audit window and the 125% usage ceiling to protect Redwood. Michael — tell us if the 125% cap or 90-day window is a blocker; procurement sometimes can be flexible on the percentage if they extend the lookback window.

-Jordan
From: Elena Vasquez <elena.vasquez@whitecap-legal.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@alturahealth.com>, procurement@alturahealth.com
Date: 2027-02-17T09:46:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Request: MSA language for phased capacity + retrospective billing parity

Hannah/Jordan — thanks for the quick draft. A couple of legal notes from Altura's side: we need (a) clearer trigger for when a tranche is considered "provisioned" (provisioning timestamp and successful endpoint checks), and (b) explicit restatement that retrospective billing parity applies only to committed-rate conversions initiated by Altura (to avoid vendor-initiated reclassifications). Small suggested edits below — I'm showing the excerpt with tracked-in-text style for clarity.

> Provisioned definition: "Provisioned" means the provisioned compute and networking are reachable at the agreed endpoint and pass the smoke-test suite referenced in Exhibit A. The provisioning timestamp is the time at which Redwood records the successful completion of the smoke-test suite in the Redwood Console.
>
> Billing parity sentence (Altura edit): "If Altura elects to convert provisioned capacity from a phased or pilot tranche to a committed tranche within ninety (90) days of provisioning, Redwood will apply the committed rate set forth in the Order Form retroactively to the date of provisioning, provided that (i) Altura's usage during the interim period does not exceed 150% of the forecasted usage for the tranche, and (ii) the conversion request is initiated by Altura and recorded in writing. Any usage beyond the 150% threshold will be billed at the standard overage rate in effect at the time of usage."

Altura's legal team prefers the 150% headroom (they've historically had bursty pilots) and wants the election to be customer-initiated. If Redwood is OK with the provisioning timestamp definition and switching the ceiling to 150% (or agreeing to a compromise like 135%), we can finalize.

I can produce a tracked-change PDF once you confirm the ceiling and the provisioning definition.

Regards,
Elena Vasquez
Counsel, Whitecap Legal (on behalf of Altura Health)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Vasquez <elena.vasquez@whitecap-legal.com>, Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@alturahealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-02-17T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: MSA language for phased capacity + retrospective billing parity

Thanks Elena — that edit is reasonable. We are open to moving the usage ceiling to 135% as a compromise (Jordan and I discussed offline) and to defining the provisioning timestamp as you suggested (Redwood Console smoke-test completion). Next steps:

1) Connor — please update the Order Form to include the proposed clause with the 135% ceiling and the provisioning definition; attach the updated change order as a new version.
2) Laura — please prep a tracked-change MSA excerpt to send to Whitecap for a final read; include Exhibit A smoke-test checklist reference.
3) Michael/Elena — once Connor uploads the updated doc, we can go to DocuSign. If Altura wants a 1-hour sign-off call before signing, we can do it tomorrow morning.

I'll hold the change order routing until Connor confirms upload. Thanks everyone — moving this to execution.

Best,
Hannah
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
